title: Legacy extraction Chromium fan-out: derived causal and instrumentation analysis

source_of_truth.private_run_log: baseline application.log, benchmark marker lines only; not committed and not reproduced here

conclusions.chromium_invocations_basis: three delegated mint calls had non-zero elapsed time and therefore missed the single-entry token cache; each cache miss performs exactly one ProcessBuilder start

candidate_extraction.note: The candidate never asks the account manager for playback proof during extraction, so the delegated provider is not called.

cold_proof_control.note: The candidate's nine browser processes belong to this explicit control, not to its production extraction. Whole-run browser unions and the helper-accounting table must not be read as candidate extraction cost.

fanout.role_evidence: The benchmark resolves /proc/<pid>/exe and reports only the basename, so all helpers collapse to 'brave'. Roles require --type and --utility-sub-type from argv; the tracer extracts only those allowlisted flags.

expected_roles.evidence: Linux Chromium forks renderers through a zygote
about:blank page plus a possible spare renderer
chrome_crashpad_handler; not observed by the name-only benchmark

benchmark_tracking_model: application PID session and process group
persistent (pid, starttime) registry for reparented/detached descendants
scope.why: The user's Brave lives in the desktop login session, not in the benchmark application's private session; the tracer additionally requires the archivetune-potoken- profile prefix and browser-lineage descent.
scope.cleanup_model: destroy the browser process and its descendants, plus Linux processes whose exact --user-data-dir matches the temporary managed profile; SIGTERM, 2 s grace, then SIGKILL
caveats: The cold-proof teardown check scans cmdline for the profile prefix; helpers that rewrite argv could make that check a false negative.
The sampler's 25 ms interval can miss a helper that calls setsid and exits before its first sample.
Category classification is name-based; any same-session process named brave/chrome would be counted, but no such process appeared outside the managed launches.

instrumentation_bias.item: delegated provider strips PO-token bindings on every currentAuthState()
instrumentation_bias.effect: forces a cold mint for every unique video even when the restored session already holds a valid bound token

instrumentation_bias.item: provider single-entry cache still serves repeat resolutions of the same video
instrumentation_bias.effect: six playback-auth calls became three launches, not six
instrumentation_bias.evidence: elapsed_ms 0 on the second call for each video; DesktopBotGuardPoTokenProvider.kt lines 71-97

instrumentation_bias.effect: warms the browser binary and OS page cache; extraction mints took 486-513 ms versus 688 ms for the first cold proof
instrumentation_bias.evidence: cold-proof elapsed 688 ms; first extraction mint 486 ms

instrumentation_bias.item: candidate arm receives the same forced cold proof
instrumentation_bias.effect: the candidate has one deliberate browser launch and nine helpers that its production extraction would never start
instrumentation_bias.evidence: candidate cold_proof browser max 9; candidate extraction browser max 0

instrumentation_bias.item: browser_processes_observed is a whole-run set of names
instrumentation_bias.effect: candidate reports 'brave' even though extraction had none
instrumentation_bias.evidence: authentication.browser_proof.browser_processes_observed is a union, not a phase metric

instrumentation_bias.item: phase boundary between cold proof and extraction
instrumentation_bias.effect: a lingering cold-proof helper could be attributed to extraction if teardown detection were wrong
instrumentation_bias.evidence: teardown-settled and extraction-begin share the same marker millisecond (cold-proof-end to teardown is 3 ms); three non-zero extraction mints independently prove new launches; browser p95 is 10 and median is 1

instrumentation_bias.effect: nine processes collapse to one name; no browser/zygote/GPU/renderer/network/crashpad attribution
instrumentation_bias.evidence: benchmark process_name() uses /proc/pid/exe basename; classify_process() is token-based

cache_semantics.cache_ttl: GenerateIT lifetime minus 10 minutes safety margin
cache_semantics.desktop_fastpath: webClientPoTokenEnabled && poTokenGvs non-blank && poTokenGvsVideoId == requested video
cache_semantics.persisted_token: secure store v4 keeps the last bound token and video id; the stored session has an expiry for session refresh, but the PO-token binding has no separate expiry and the fastpath does not check one
cache_semantics.cross_video_session_token: resolveGvsPoToken() falls back to poTokenGvsSession for non-WEB_CREATOR clients that use Web proof; native clients such as VISIONOS do not use Web proof, but DesktopSessionManager still mints for each new video
cache_semantics.forced_cold_wrapper: the benchmark hides every binding, so the fastpath and persisted token can never be used in either arm

necessity.required_for_web_client_proof: conditional and not proven by this run
necessity.avoidable_by_lazy_mint_on_403: candidate design option; not implemented or measured
necessity.why_observed_resolution_did_not_need_it: all six baseline rows resolved through VISIONOS 0.1, while the token was minted for the WEB_REMIX preference; the candidate resolved the same videos via yt-dlp with zero browser processes

recommendations.action: Add a warm-policy arm that does not strip persisted bindings, and mark each provider cache hit/miss explicitly.
recommendations.reason: Separates production steady-state from the forced cold worst case.

recommendations.action: Run scripts/trace-legacy-browser.py in attach mode during one real mint and in controlled launch mode.
recommendations.reason: Confirms the role mix, ancestry edges, lifetime, and teardown without recording argv.

recommendations.action: Preserve and exercise the existing per-video token fastpath; do not let a resolver change clear valid bindings.
recommendations.reason: This is the only browser-free path that still provides Web proof when a token is already valid.

recommendations.action: Evaluate lazy proof: resolve with the existing session/native clients, and mint per-video proof only after a concrete 403 from a Web client.
recommendations.reason: prepareStreamHttpRecovery already implements the retry path; the observed VISIONOS success suggests eager proof may be unnecessary for many tracks.

recommendations.action: Evaluate session-token reuse for clients that accept session-bound GVS proof before minting a new per-video token.
recommendations.reason: resolveGvsPoToken already treats poTokenGvsSession as valid for non-WEB_CREATOR clients.

recommendations.action: Consider a small bounded multi-entry cache to avoid A,B,A thrash and preloader churn.
recommendations.reason: A single entry re-launches on alternating videos; a queue preloader can trigger mints ahead of playback.

acceptance_criteria: one browser root and at least one zygote/renderer/utility edge
crashpad presence recorded as 0 or 1 rather than assumed
zero leftovers and profile removed after teardown
no argv, URL, cookie, profile path, or environment value in the JSON

open_questions: Exact per-role counts for one Brave 155 headless invocation on this host.
Whether crashpad starts in headless mode or exits before the first sample.
Whether the production warm policy would have skipped zero, one, or three of the observed mints.
Whether WEB_REMIX actually needed the minted proof, or simply lost the race to VISIONOS.
Whether the next-stream preloader triggers additional mints during playback outside the measured phase.
